- the addition of IPv6 fields and backward compatibility with the older PAPI protocol version (maybe it was clarified in the older merge request but we do not have the discussions here
- dissect_ubt() has a wrong signature (it should return an int and not a boolean)

the proto_tree_add_bitmask() function. In addition, it allows to:
- Provide a leading text (e.g. "Flags: ") that will appear before

There are the following flags defined:

  BMT_NO_APPEND - the title is taken "as-is" from the 'name' argument.

  BMT_NO_FALSE - boolean flags are only added to the title if they are set.
  BMT_NO_TFS - only add flag name to the title, do not use true_false_string

The proto_tree_add_bitmask_with_flags() function is an extended version
of the proto_tree_add_bitmask() function. It allows using flags to specify
which fields will affect the top-level title. The flags are the
same BMT_NO_* flags as used in the proto_tree_add_bitmask_text() function.

Here is the TLV for SeverIP as displayed in Wireshark when run:
![ServerIP](/uploads/861a1187265a504bbc3abc6088963f6d/ServerIP.png)
but missing to display val ? (and some extra reserved bytes ?)

![ServerIP_Long_Format](/uploads/391940161cac02eaa34c6a72b4f38fb2/ServerIP_Long_Format.png)
Hi! As you can see in the image above, the ServerIP field alone is 20 bytes long. Out of which, the first two bytes are stored in val which helps us determine if the IP address is of type IPv4 or IPv6. The next two bytes are just plain padding which is always zero and to be ignored. Now, depending on the type, it reads the next 4 bytes (if IPv4) or next 16 bytes (if IPv6). In the example above, we can see the type to be IPv4, which is why it reads the four bytes, displays the IP address and ignores the rest of the following bytes. This is the way how IP addresses are structured in UBT protocol. Now, as you can see, val is just used to determine the type of IP address. Now, is there a necessity to display the val itself as the user can determine if it's IPv4 or IPv6 from the address itself as displayed here below:
![ServerIP](/uploads/d8c1104028e8594e17767cb843702245/ServerIP.png)

You need to display ALL bytes like this : 

```
Type: 17
Val: 02 (IPv4)
Padding: 0000
Server IP Address (IPv4): X.X.X.X
Padding: 0000000
```

There are four IP address fields (SAC IP Address, UAC IP Address in Nodelist, UAC IP Address in Bucketmap and Server IP Address) which use the same format. So, should all four fields be displayed as such?
Yes
